{{Start date and age|df=yes|1900}} (as a football association) | ground = [[Planet Group Arena]] | capacity = 20,175[http://www.kaagent.be/nl/stadium/updates/ De Ghelamco Arena] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160627003722/http://www.kaagent.be/nl/stadium/updates/ |date=27 June 2016 }} kaagent.be (last check 30 March 2018) | owntitle = Chairman | owner = [[Sam Baro]] | chrtitle = Sporting Director | chairman = [[Arnar Viðarsson]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Rik De Mil]] | league = {{Belgian football updater|KAAGent}} | season = {{Belgian football updater|KAAGent2}} | position = {{Belgian football updater|KAAGent3}} | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _gent2425h | pattern_b1 = _gent2425h | pattern_ra1 = _gent2425h | pattern_sh1 = _gent2425h | pattern_so1 = _gent2425hl | leftarm1 = 0023DD | body1 = 0023DD | rightarm1 = 0023DD | shorts1 = 0023DD | socks1 = 0023DD | pattern_la2 = _gent2425a | pattern_b2 = _gent2425a | pattern_ra2 = _gent2425a | pattern_sh2 = _gent2425a | pattern_so2 = _gent2425al | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _gent2425t | pattern_b3 = _gent2425t | pattern_ra3 = _gent2425t | pattern_sh3 = _gent2425t | pattern_so3 = _gent2425al | leftarm3 = f0ff0f | body3 = f0ff0f | rightarm3 = f0ff0f | shorts3 = f0ff0f | socks3 = f0ff0f | current = 2026–27 KAA Gent season }} '''Koninklijke Atletiek Associatie Gent''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈkoːnɪŋkləkə ʔɑtləˈtik ɑsoːˈɕaːsi ˈɣɛnt}}; English: ''Royal Athletic Association Ghent''), often simply known as '''Gent''' or by their nickname '''''{{notatypo|De Buffalo's}}''''' ({{langx|en|The Buffalos}}), is a Belgian professional [[sports club]], based in the city of [[Ghent]], [[East Flanders]]. Their [[Association football|football]] team is the best known section within the club and has been playing in the [[Belgian First Division A]] since the [[1989–90 Belgian First Division|1989–90 season]]. They won the national league once, in [[2014–15 Belgian Pro League|2014–15]], in addition to four [[Belgian Cup]] victories. Gent played their home matches in the [[Jules Ottenstadion]] in [[Gentbrugge]] from 1920 until 2013, when they moved to the [[Ghelamco Arena|Planet Group Arena]]. Their team colours are blue and white. The principal sponsor is Baloise, with Hamann International Logistics sponsoring for the [[UEFA Conference League]] matches. The field hockey and track and field divisions were founded in 1864, making it one of the oldest sports clubs in [[Belgium]]. The club was then known under its French name '''La Gantoise''' (and it is still referred to as such in the French-speaking part of Belgium). They changed their name to the current Dutch version in 1971. The football division opened in 1900. The nickname of the club is ''{{notatypo|De Buffalo's}}'', a term coined after a visit of the original [[Buffalo Bill]] and his [[Wild West shows|Wild West circus]] to the city in the early 20th century.{{Cite web|url=https://playingfor90.com/2016/02/18/kaa-gent-unusual-nickname/|title = KAA Gent and Their Unusual Nickname|date = 18 February 2016}} Their logo features a [[Native Americans in the United States|Native American]] in profile. The origins of this logo are attributed to the feather headdresses worn by the Indian chiefs who performed with Buffalo Bill, though this logo has [[Native American mascot controversy|garnered some controversy]] in recent years.{{Cite web | title=Logo | url=https://www.kaagent.be/en/our-club/logo | website=KA Gent | access-date=October 3, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200828170514/https://www.kaagent.be/en/our-club/logo | archive-date=August 28, 2020 }}{{Cite web | last=Rhodin | first=Alexander | date=May 7, 2018 | title=Native American Mascots Live On in Europe | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/07/sports/native-american-mascots-europe.html | website=The New York Times | access-date=October 3, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507123456/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/07/sports/native-american-mascots-europe.html | archive-date=May 7, 2018 }} Gent enjoyed its first spell at the highest level in Belgian football between [[1913–14 Belgian First Division|1913–14]] and [[1928–29 Belgian First Division|1928–29]], and a second one from [[1936–37 Belgian First Division|1936–37]] to [[1966–67 Belgian First Division|1966–67]]. In the 1970s and 1980s, the club had several promotions and relegations between the first and [[Belgian Second Division|second]] divisions, before returning to the highest level in 1989. The club reached the quarter-finals of the [[1991–92 UEFA Cup]], which is their best achievement ever in European competitions. Aside from [[Association football|football]], Gent also have other sports sections in [[track and field]] and [[field hockey]]."}}
